Q: Orval intermittently returns 403 when fetching Swagger via Nginx reverse proxy in GitHub Actions A:

What I’ve confirmed

  • Orval itself does not support proxy configuration (expected)

  • Axios proxy config is irrelevant (browser/runtime only)

  • The request reaches Nginx (not DNS / network failure)

  • Backend works fine when accessed directly

  • The issue only happens in CI (GitHub Actions)

Suspicions

This seems related to Nginx rules such as:

  • rate limiting

  • IP-based rules

  • bot / User-Agent filtering

  • auth/session expectations

  • WAF or security rules

Since GitHub Actions uses rotating IPs and non-browser User-Agents, some requests appear to be blocked.

Question

What is the correct way to expose Swagger via Nginx so that:

  • Orval can reliably fetch it from CI (GitHub Actions)

  • Production API security is not weakened

  • Intermittent 403s are avoided

Specifically:

  • Should Swagger be exposed via a separate Nginx location?

  • Should auth / rate limits be disabled for Swagger?

  • Are there recommended Nginx headers or rules for CI clients?

Expected outcome

A stable, CI-safe setup where Orval can fetch Swagger through an Nginx reverse proxy without random 403 errors.

Q: "Transparent" function: perfectly forwarding an argument to the return value A:

Your function is already correct (or as correct as possible). The test cases that you marked not ok also don't compile without the function, so there is no issue here.

There are some other cases where there is difference, but those are impossible to fix:

  • C &&c = manipulate(C{}); doesn't extend the lifetime of the temporary, but it would without the function.

  • C c = manipulate(C{}); requires one move, and doesn't compile if C is non-movable. Without the function, the copy would've been elided (so there would be 0 moves, and the class wouldn't be required to be movable).

Q: Why is `sort` not working in this example? A:

The first key -k1 defaults from field 1 to the end of the line, so it's necessary to specify the end position of the primary key.

echo -e "25:Oct\n26:Jan\n25:Sep\n24:Nov" | sort -t':' -k1,1n -k2,2M

In this code, the end positions are specified, and I believe this code will work correctly.
